title: Korean Quality Assurance Lead (QAL)
description:
In this hourly, remote contractor role, you will work as a Korean Quality Assurance Lead (QAL) to oversee quality, consistency, and trainer performance across Korean AI training projects. You will review AI-generated Korean content and trainer/QA work, evaluate output quality against project guidelines, provide precise written feedback, and ensure that all contributors follow the expected quality standards.

You will assess work for accuracy, fluency, grammar, spelling, tone, cultural appropriateness, meaning preservation, instruction-following, formatting, and adherence to project-specific rubrics. You will spot recurring quality issues, communicate updates to trainers and QAs, support onboarding, maintain documentation, and help activate contributors who are not working consistently. This role requires strong Korean and English skills, excellent attention to detail, structured communication, and the ability to manage quality workflows across remote teams.

This role is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI Data Services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate, delivering training data for many of the world’s largest AI companies and foundation-model labs. Your Korean quality leadership will directly help improve the world’s premier AI models by ensuring that Korean training data is natural, accurate, culturally appropriate, well-documented, and aligned with client expectations.

Selection process involves an AI interview, a domain-specific task, and an interview with a recruiter.

Important:
There is no immediate project for this role; however, if qualified, you will be among the first experts we reach out to when relevant opportunities arise. This will also provide you with access to future projects available through our expert network.

Requirements:

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Korean, Linguistics, Translation, Communications, Journalism, English, Education, Quality Assurance, or a relevant domain/related field.
- Native or near-native Korean proficiency with strong reading and writing skills.
- Strong grasp of the English language to follow project guidelines, communicate with teams, and provide clear feedback in English.
- 3+ years of professional experience in Korean writing, editing, translation, localization, content QA, AI training, education, annotation, or related language-review workflows.
- Strong understanding of Korean grammar, spelling conventions, punctuation, honorifics, speech levels, tone, register, and cultural context.
- Ability to evaluate Korean content against detailed rubrics and identify issues such as mistranslation, literal phrasing, unnatural tone, incorrect honorifics, hallucinated claims, ambiguity, or inconsistent terminology.
- Comfortable handling formal vs informal Korean, honorific usage, product/UI localization terminology, and audience adaptation for South Korean users.
- Experience leading or supporting remote teams of trainers, annotators, reviewers, editors, or QAs is strongly preferred.
- Comfortable working in fast-moving remote environments using tools such as Discord, Google Sheets, Google Docs, trackers, dashboards, and project management systems.
- Highly detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to maintain style guides, FAQs, trackers, onboarding materials, honeypots, and other quality documentation.
- Experience with AI training, data annotation, large language models, prompt/response evaluation, or rubric-based LLM QA is a strong plus.

Responsibilities:

- Quality monitoring: Spot-check Korean items, identify quality issues, provide ongoing feedback through DMs, and escalate recurring or critical issues.
- Trainer and QA communication: Update trainers and QAs on Discord about new item guidelines, project changes, workflow updates, and quality expectations.
- Question handling: Respond to trainer/QA questions clearly and promptly, especially around Korean wording, honorifics, speech level, register, translation fidelity, cultural context, and edge cases.
- Trainer/QA activation management: DM contributors who are inactive or not working, encourage activation, track follow-ups, and flag availability issues when needed.
- Documentation: Create and maintain Korean project documentation, including style guides, trackers, FAQs, quality notes, examples, honeypots, and onboarding materials.
- Onboarding and training: Schedule and run onboarding/training calls with trainers and QAs to explain project expectations, workflows, rubrics, quality standards, and Korean-specific style requirements.
- Quality alignment: Ensure all trainers and QAs apply Korean language guidelines consistently and understand updates as projects evolve.
- Process improvement: Identify recurring quality gaps, propose workflow improvements, and help build scalable QA processes for Korean-language projects.

title: Korean Language Expert
description:
In this hourly-paid, fully remote contractor role, you will review AI-generated responses and/or generate language content, evaluate reasoning quality and step-by-step problem-solving, and provide expert feedback so outputs are accurate, logical, and clearly explained. You will assess solutions for accuracy, clarity, and adherence to the prompt; identify errors in methodology or conceptual understanding; fact-check information; write high-quality explanations and model solutions that demonstrate correct methods; and rate and compare multiple AI responses based on correctness and reasoning quality. You will apply senior-level Korean localization/translation judgment alongside Minimum C1 English proficiency to ensure terminology, tone, and cultural nuance are consistently correct across use cases. This role is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI Data Services company and a subsidiary of SuperAnnotate that provides AI training data for many of the world’s largest AI companies and foundation-model labs. Your work directly helps improve the world’s premier AI models.

Important:
There is no immediate project for this role; however, if qualified, you will be among the first experts we reach out to when relevant opportunities arise. This will also provide you with access to future projects available through our expert network.

Requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree or higher in Translation, Linguistics, Localization, Communications, or a related field.
- Native or near-native Korean proficiency and strong command of the locale conventions for South Korea.
- Minimum C1 English proficiency (reading/writing) for interpreting prompts, sources, and evaluation guidelines.
- 5+ years of professional localization/translation experience (multilingual localization experience strongly preferred).
- Demonstrated ability to apply MQM/LQA concepts (severity, category, and root-cause thinking) to produce consistent quality decisions.
- Proficiency with CAT tools and QA workflows (translation memory, termbases, automated checks) and comfort working with structured guidelines.
- Excellent editorial judgment (register, tone, inclusivity, and cultural nuance) with extreme attention to detail.
- Ability to rigorously fact-check localized content (units, references, names, dates) using reliable sources and consistent reasoning.
- Comfort working as an hourly contractor: dependable throughput, clear documentation, and responsiveness across time zones.
- Previous experience with AI data training / annotation / evaluation is preferred.
- Location requirement: Only candidates based in South Korea will be considered for this role

Responsibilities:

- Develop AI Training Content: Create detailed prompts in various topics and responses to guide AI learning, ensuring the models reflect a comprehensive understanding of diverse subjects.
- Optimize AI Performance: Evaluate and rank AI responses to enhance the model's accuracy, fluency, and contextual relevance.
- Ensure Model Integrity: Test AI models for potential inaccuracies or biases, validating their reliability across use cases.

description:

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Dutch, Linguistics, Translation, Communications, Journalism, English, Education, Quality Assurance, or a relevant domain/related field.
- Native or near-native Dutch proficiency with strong reading and writing skills.
- Strong grasp of the English language to follow project guidelines, communicate with teams, and provide clear feedback in English.
- 3+ years of professional experience in Dutch writing, editing, translation, localization, content QA, AI training, education, annotation, or related language-review workflows.
- Strong understanding of Dutch grammar, spelling conventions, punctuation, tone, register, business writing norms, and cultural context.
- Comfortable handling variation as needed: Netherlands Dutch and/or Belgian Dutch (Flemish), including tone and vocabulary differences. Candidates should specify which variant(s) they can support.

- Experience leading or supporting remote teams of trainers, annotators, reviewers, editors, or QAs is strongly preferred.
- Comfortable working in fast-moving remote environments using tools such as Discord, Google Sheets, Google Docs, trackers, dashboards, and project management systems.
- Highly detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to maintain style guides, FAQs, trackers, onboarding materials, honeypots, and other quality documentation.

title: Workforce Experience Specialists
description:
# About SuperAnnotate

SuperAnnotate helps the world’s leading AI teams build responsible, next-generation models powered by high-quality human data. We’re a fast-growing Series B startup bridging the gap between advanced AI innovation and the data that drives it. Our global network of expert specialists, scalable managed operations, precise talent matching, and full project transparency ensure unmatched data quality at scale. Trusted by innovators like Databricks and ServiceNow - and backed by NVIDIA, Dell Technologies Capital, Databricks Ventures, Cox Enterprises, and Lionel Messi’s Play Time VC - SuperAnnotate is proud to be the top-ranked AI data company on G2 for multiple consecutive years, including 2025.

# About the team

SME Careers is our platform for recruiting, onboarding and paying the domain experts and annotators behind our AI projects. The team works across Dhaka, Armenia and the United States. Our Mirpur DOHS office in Dhaka is home to core engineering, workforce experience, forward-deployed engineering and part of project management. You'll be part of the Dhaka team, with hybrid and remote work supported. You'll report to a manager in San Francisco and work regularly with our teams in the US and Europe.

# The role

From the moment someone applies to SME Careers until they're paid for their work, you're the person they come to when something goes wrong. That might be a stuck application, a missing interview invite, a confusing guideline, lost platform access or a late payment. You fix it or route it to the right team, notice when the same problem keeps happening, and keep projects moving. The job will be contracted through our local partner in Bangladesh.

# What you'll do

- Help applicants and contractors at every stage, from application, assessment and onboarding through project work and payments, using Slack, Discord and our support tools.
- Resolve issues with Talent, Engineering, Finance and project leads. Escalate clearly when something needs a decision.
- Keep an eye on project progress and contractor capacity, and help reassign work when a project falls behind.
- Spot recurring problems and turn them into fixes: better FAQs, templates, SOPs or guideline updates.
- Keep issue tracking and handover notes clean so nothing slips between shifts.

# Your first weeks
You'll shadow the Dhaka team, learn our platform and project workflows, and start handling applicant and contractor questions on your own by week three or four.

# What you'll bring

- 1–3 years in support, community or operations, ideally at an AI data, tech or BPO company.
- Excellent written English. Most of your work is written communication with contractors around the world.
- Comfort managing several workstreams in spreadsheets and tools like Slack, Discord or Jira.
- A habit of noticing when something's off and chasing it until it's fixed.
- Nice to have: data annotation or QA experience, a basic understanding of LLMs, Python or advanced Sheets formulas.

# Schedule

We support projects around the clock. You'll work 5 days a week on a rotating roster that can include weekends and night shifts. Shifts are published in advance.

# Salary and benefits

- BDT 35,000–50,000 per month, based on skills and experience

title: Explosives & Energetic Materials Expert for AI Safety Audit
description:
## Description

SME Careers is hiring explosives and energetic materials professionals to audit how AI models respond to sensitive questions in the field. Each task gives you a user request and the answers three different models gave to it. You classify the request (benign, dual-use or adversarial), mark each answer as safe or unsafe and say why, rank the three against each other, and write the answer the model should have given. For dual-use requests you also note what makes it sensitive, what legitimate purpose it serves, and who should be able to get an answer.

The requests are realistic: what mining and blasting engineers, pyrotechnicians, propellant chemists, bomb technicians, investigators and occasionally bad actors actually ask. Some are ordinary professional questions that models wrongly refuse, and catching those matters as much as catching the dangerous ones.

## Who we're looking for

Commercial blasting engineers and mining/quarry explosives specialists; military or police EOD and bomb technicians; energetic materials, propellant or pyrotechnics chemists; post-blast investigators and forensic examiners; explosives safety officers and regulators (ATF, HSE, DoD explosives safety, or equivalent). Usually a relevant degree or certification plus five or more years of hands-on professional experience. Experience writing incident reports, safety cases or expert opinions is a strong plus.

## Before you apply

Open only to citizens or permanent residents of the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and The European Union

Requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree or higher in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Energetic Materials, Explosives Engineering, Safety Engineering, Hazardous Materials Management, Environmental Health & Safety, or a closely related field; advanced degree or professional safety certification is a strong plus.
- 3+ years of professional experience in explosives safety, energetic materials, hazardous materials safety, chemical safety, defense safety, industrial safety, EHS, regulatory compliance, risk assessment, technical safety review, or related work.
- Strong understanding of explosives and energetic materials safety concepts, including hazard classification, sensitivity, compatibility, storage principles, transport considerations, environmental conditions, blast/fire risk, and safe handling frameworks.
- Familiarity with safety documentation and frameworks such as Safety Data Sheets, GHS hazard communication, hazardous materials classification, SOPs, risk assessments, incident escalation procedures, and applicable safety/regulatory guidance.
- Ability to review AI-generated explosives or energetic-materials content for technical accuracy, safety alignment, misuse risk, inappropriate specificity, hallucinated claims, and potentially dangerous procedural guidance.
- Strong judgment in distinguishing between safe high-level educational or safety content and content that could enable unsafe handling, synthesis, acquisition, weaponization, evasion, or harmful experimentation.
- Excellent written English skills, with the ability to provide clear, structured feedback explaining why a response is safe, unsafe, incomplete, misleading, or technically incorrect.
- High attention to detail when reviewing terminology, hazard categories, material properties, units, risk assumptions, safety controls, storage/transport considerations, and emergency-response guidance.
- Comfortable applying detailed project rubrics consistently across ambiguous or sensitive scenarios involving explosives, energetic materials, pyrotechnics, propellants, reactive chemicals, or hazardous mixtures.
- Prior experience with AI safety, red-team review, model evaluation, content moderation, data annotation, technical QA, scientific review, EHS review, hazardous-materials review, or rubric-based evaluation is preferred.

Responsibilities:

- Develop AI Training Content: Create detailed prompts in various topics and responses to guide AI learning, ensuring the models reflect a comprehensive understanding of diverse subjects.
- Optimize AI Performance: Evaluate and rank AI responses to enhance the model's accuracy, fluency, and contextual relevance.
- Ensure Model Integrity: Test AI models for potential inaccuracies or biases, validating their reliability across use cases.

title: CBRN Specialist
description:
In this hourly, remote contractor role, you will work as a CBRN Specialist (SME) to review AI-generated content related to chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear safety topics and/or create high-quality reference content that supports safe, accurate, policy-aligned AI behavior. You will evaluate technical accuracy, safety framing, terminology, risk awareness, and reasoning quality while providing precise written feedback.

You will assess outputs for correctness, clarity, responsible handling of hazardous topics, appropriate refusal/redirection where needed, and adherence to project guidelines. You will identify errors in CBRN terminology, hazard classification, emergency preparedness, exposure risk, protective measures, public-safety communication, regulatory framing, and scientific interpretation. You will also flag unsafe, operationally enabling, misleading, or overconfident content and help ensure that model responses remain useful without providing dangerous instructions.

This role is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI Data Services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate, delivering training data for many of the world’s largest AI companies and foundation-model labs. Your CBRN expertise directly helps improve the world’s premier AI models by making their responses safer, more accurate, more responsible, and better aligned with public-safety expectations.

Requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree or higher in Chemistry, Biology, Microbiology, Public Health, Toxicology, Nuclear Engineering, Radiation Science, Emergency Management, Environmental Health & Safety, Biosecurity, Security Studies, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
- Strong professional proficiency in English, minimum C1, to follow guidelines and provide detailed written feedback in English.
- 3+ years of professional experience in CBRN safety, emergency preparedness, hazardous materials, biosafety, radiation safety, public health, environmental health and safety, defense/security analysis, technical review, or related work.
- Strong understanding of chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear hazard categories, including safe high-level risk assessment, exposure pathways, protective concepts, emergency communication, and public-safety principles.
- Ability to evaluate CBRN-related AI outputs for accuracy, safety, completeness, policy alignment, and potential misuse risk.
- Comfortable identifying unsafe instructions, operationally enabling details, inappropriate specificity, misleading hazard claims, inaccurate emergency advice, or unsupported technical conclusions.
- Familiarity with safety frameworks, emergency-response concepts, biosafety levels, hazardous-material communication, radiation protection principles, decontamination concepts, incident reporting, and public-health guidance is preferred.
- High attention to detail when reviewing terminology, units, exposure concepts, risk levels, safety disclaimers, escalation guidance, and sensitive technical boundaries.
- Reliable, self-directed, and able to deliver consistent quality in an hourly, remote contractor workflow across time zones.
- Prior experience with AI safety, data annotation, technical QA, policy review, risk assessment, red-team review, scientific review, or rubric-based evaluation is strongly preferred.

- Review CBRN-related AI content: Evaluate AI-generated responses involving chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, hazardous-material, emergency-preparedness, and public-safety topics for accuracy, safety, and guideline alignment.
- Identify unsafe or enabling content: Flag outputs that provide dangerous procedural detail, acquisition guidance, weaponization support, evasion tactics, unsafe lab guidance, harmful exposure advice, or other misuse-enabling content.
- Develop safe reference content: Create gold-standard examples that answer benign CBRN questions responsibly while avoiding operationally dangerous instructions.
- Optimize AI safety behavior: Evaluate and rank model outputs based on safe handling, correct risk framing, appropriate refusals, helpful redirection, scientific accuracy, and clarity.
- Ensure model integrity: Detect hallucinated claims, incorrect hazard classifications, misleading risk statements, overconfident conclusions, poor escalation guidance, or unsafe recommendations.

- Maintain technical quality: Ensure CBRN-related content uses precise terminology, avoids exaggeration or minimization of risks, and communicates safety information in a responsible, user-appropriate way.
- Escalate sensitive cases: Flag ambiguous, high-risk, or potentially harmful content for additional review according to project guidelines.

title: Nuclear & Radiological Safety Expert for AI Model Audit
description:
## Description

SME Careers is assembling a small panel of nuclear and radiological professionals to audit how AI models respond to sensitive questions in the field. Each task gives you a user request and the answers three different models gave to it. You classify the request (benign, dual-use or adversarial), mark each answer as safe or unsafe and say why, rank the three against each other, and write the answer the model should have given. For dual-use requests you also note what makes it sensitive, what legitimate purpose it serves, and who should be able to get an answer.

The requests are realistic: the kinds of things reactor engineers, health physicists, regulators, students and occasionally bad actors actually ask. Some are ordinary professional questions that models wrongly refuse, and catching those matters as much as catching the dangerous ones.

This role is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI Data Services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate, delivering training data for many of the world’s largest AI companies and foundation-model labs. Your nuclear physics expertise directly helps improve the world’s leading AI models by making their nuclear science, radiation, and physics outputs more accurate, safe and reliable.

## Who we're looking for

Nuclear engineers and reactor physicists, safeguards and nonproliferation specialists (IAEA, NRC or equivalent, export control, national labs), health physicists and radiation safety officers, radiochemists, and former military or government nuclear personnel. Usually a relevant degree plus five or more years of professional experience. Experience reviewing technical work against a standard (licensing, inspection, peer review) or AI red teaming is a strong plus.

## Before you apply

This role is open only to citizens or residents of the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and the European Union.

title: Chemical Safety Expert for AI Model Safety Audit
description:
## Description

SME Careers is hiring chemists and chemical safety professionals to audit how AI models respond to sensitive questions in the field. Each task gives you a user request and the answers three different models gave to it. You classify the request (benign, dual-use or adversarial), mark each answer as safe or unsafe and say why, rank the three against each other, and write the answer the model should have given. For dual-use requests you also note what makes it sensitive, what legitimate purpose it serves, and who should be able to get an answer.

The requests are realistic: what synthetic and analytical chemists, toxicologists, industrial hygienists, process safety engineers, regulators and occasionally bad actors actually ask. Some are ordinary professional questions that models wrongly refuse, and catching those matters as much as catching the dangerous ones.

## Who we're looking for

Synthetic and analytical chemists; toxicologists and pharmacologists; industrial hygienists and chemical safety/process safety professionals; CWC or chemical-security specialists; hazmat, poison-control or chemical incident responders; and chemical regulators (EPA, OSHA, HSE, OPCW-adjacent, or equivalent). Usually a relevant degree plus five or more years of professional experience. Experience with safety data sheets, exposure assessment, incident reports or regulatory review is a strong plus.

## Before you apply

Open only to citizens or permanent residents of the US, UK, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and the European Union.

Requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree or higher in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Toxicology, Environmental Health & Safety, Industrial Hygiene, Hazardous Materials Management, or a closely related field; advanced degree or professional safety certification is a strong plus.
- 3+ years of professional experience in chemical safety, laboratory safety, hazardous materials handling, EHS, toxicology, industrial hygiene, chemical risk assessment, regulatory compliance, or related technical safety work.
- Strong understanding of chemical hazards, including toxicity, corrosivity, flammability, reactivity, incompatibilities, exposure routes, storage risks, spill response principles, PPE, ventilation, and safe handling practices.
- Familiarity with chemical safety documentation and frameworks such as Safety Data Sheets, GHS hazard communication, labeling, exposure limits, risk assessments, SOPs, and incident escalation procedures.
- Ability to review AI-generated chemical safety content for technical accuracy, safety alignment, misuse risk, hallucinated claims, inappropriate specificity, and potentially dangerous procedural guidance.
- Strong judgment in distinguishing between safe educational content and content that could enable unsafe chemical handling, synthesis, misuse, evasion, or harmful experimentation.
- Excellent written English skills, with the ability to provide clear, structured feedback explaining why a response is safe, unsafe, incomplete, misleading, or technically incorrect.
- High attention to detail when reviewing chemical terminology, units, concentrations, exposure assumptions, hazard classifications, safety controls, and emergency-response guidance.
- Comfortable applying detailed project rubrics consistently across ambiguous or sensitive chemical safety scenarios.
- Prior experience with AI safety, red-team review, model evaluation, content moderation, data annotation, technical QA, scientific review, or rubric-based evaluation is preferred.

Responsibilities:

- Develop AI Training Content: Create detailed prompts in various topics and responses to guide AI learning, ensuring the models reflect a comprehensive understanding of diverse subjects.
- Optimize AI Performance: Evaluate and rank AI responses to enhance the model's accuracy, fluency, and contextual relevance.
- Ensure Model Integrity: Test AI models for potential inaccuracies or biases, validating their reliability across use cases.

In this hourly, remote contractor role, you will work as a Thai Language Specialist (SME) to review AI-generated Thai content and/or create high-quality Thai reference content, evaluating language quality and step-by-step reasoning while providing precise written feedback. You will assess outputs for accuracy, fluency, grammar, spelling, tone, cultural appropriateness, and adherence to the prompt; identify errors in meaning, mistranslation, register (formal vs informal), ambiguity, politeness particles/levels, and logical consistency; fact-check claims when needed; write high-quality rewrites and model answers that demonstrate best practices in Thai writing; and rate and compare multiple AI responses based on correctness and overall quality.

This role is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI Data Services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate, delivering training data for many of the world’s largest AI companies and foundation-model labs. Your Thai expertise directly helps improve the world’s premier AI models by making their Thai language output more natural, reliable, culturally accurate, and clearly written.

Important: There is no immediate project for this role; however, if qualified, you will be among the first experts we reach out to when relevant opportunities arise. This will also provide you with access to future projects available through our expert network.

Requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Linguistics, Thai/English Literature, Communications, Journalism, Translation, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).
- Native or near-native Thai proficiency (reading and writing required).
- Strong professional proficiency in English (minimum C1) to follow guidelines and provide detailed feedback in English.
- 3+ years of professional experience in writing, editing, localization, translation, content QA, journalism, education, or related language-focused work.
- Deep understanding of Thai writing conventions: spelling, punctuation, segmentation/word spacing practices, and tone/register—able to explain why something is wrong and how to fix it.
- Comfortable handling Thai politeness and formality levels (e.g., particles like ครับ/ค่ะ, respectful phrasing) and adapting to different audiences (customer support vs casual).
- High attention to detail when spotting subtle meaning shifts, awkward literal translations, hallucinated claims, or culturally mismatched phrasing.
- Reliable, self-directed, and able to deliver consistent quality in an hourly, remote contractor workflow across time zones.
- Prior experience with AI data training/annotation, translation QA, editorial QA, or rubric-based evaluation is strongly preferred.

Responsibilities:

- Develop AI Training Content: Create prompts and gold-standard Thai answers across multiple domains (general knowledge, customer support, education, conversational writing).
- Optimize AI Performance: Evaluate and rank AI outputs to improve fluency, correctness, tone match, and cultural appropriateness.
- Ensure Model Integrity: Detect unsafe or misleading content, factual hallucinations, bias, and policy-risk language; validate reliability across use cases.

title: FreeCAD / Mechanical CAD Expert, AI Computer-Use Trainer
description:
## About SME Careers

As AI systems become more sophisticated, they rely on human knowledge to better understand context and the world. At SME Careers, we partner with leading AI labs to improve how the next generation of intelligent systems learn, reason, and act. SME Careers is a fast-growing AI data services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate that provides AI training data to many of the world's top AI companies and foundation model labs. Your expertise in parametric CAD will directly help improve the world's premier AI models.

## About the Role

AI agents are getting good at reading a screen and clicking through web forms. Put one in front of a parametric CAD package and it falls apart. FreeCAD is an unforgiving test case: multiple workbenches with overlapping capabilities, a constraint solver that fails in ways the interface doesn't explain, feature histories where the correct next action depends entirely on what was built twenty steps earlier, and the topological naming problem lying in wait for anyone who references geometry carelessly. Engineering intent lives in the model tree, not on the screen — and that is exactly what current agents cannot see.

In this remote, hourly contract role you will help close that gap. You will design realistic, challenging CAD tasks, then record yourself completing them on your own computer using recording tools we provide. Each recording captures the full picture of how expert work actually gets done, the sequence of actions, the interface state at every step, and the files before and after, and becomes both a demonstration the model learns from and a benchmark it is measured against.

Because a model can only learn from work that can be scored, an equally important part of the job is defining what "done correctly" means. Alongside each task you will write the objective and the steps you took, and specify how the result should be verified, what the finished part, sketch, assembly, or drawing has to satisfy for the outcome to count as correct, and which intermediate checkpoints a partially-successful attempt would hit. In CAD this is a sharper question than it looks: a part can be dimensionally correct and still be wrong, because the sketch is under-constrained, the feature order won't survive a parameter change, or the model references a face that will migrate the moment anything upstream is edited. Encoding that distinction, dimensionally right versus actually right, is the contribution we need from you.

This position is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI data services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate that provides AI training data to many of the world's top AI companies and foundation model labs. Your work will directly help improve the world's premier AI models.

## What You'll Do
- Author production-realistic CAD tasks: Write task briefs reflecting work an engineering team would actually assign, model a part to a dimensioned drawing, build a parametric family driven by a spreadsheet, assemble components with mating constraints, produce a TechDraw sheet with sections and tolerances, prepare geometry for manufacture or export, scoped tightly enough that the outcome can be objectively verified.
- Record expert demonstrations: Set up your own environment for the task (reference drawings, source files, workbenches and add-ons in place) and record yourself executing it end to end with the provided capture tooling, producing a complete trace of actions, interface state, and file changes.-
- Document the workflow step by step: Log the steps you took in a form another engineer could follow and reproduce, in clear professional English.
- Define verification and success criteria: Specify what the finished model must satisfy, dimensional correctness, fully-constrained sketches, robust feature references, a tree that survives a parameter change, plus the intermediate milestones that mark real progress and the plausible wrong paths that should not be credited.
- Cover the range of difficulty: Produce tasks from single sketch-and-pad operations up to long, multi-step workflows that cross applications (a drawing opened from a PDF, dimensions pulled from a spreadsheet, output handed to a slicer, mesh or STEP data round-tripped from another tool).
- Review and quality-check others' work: For those who move into QA, audit submitted traces for task realism, recording completeness, step-to-action mapping, and whether the stated success criteria genuinely hold for the model produced.
- Work to project quality standards: Keep recordings free of personal information and confidential client geometry, use only approved applications, and complete all work using your own expertise, the use of closed-source AI assistants is contractually prohibited on this project.

## What You Bring
- 2–5 years of professional experience in mechanical design, product development, manufacturing engineering, or a comparable CAD-centric role (contract, studio, in-house, or freelance).
- Genuine FreeCAD proficiency, not just general CAD experience. You work fluently in Sketcher and Part Design, understand the difference between the Part and Part Design approaches and when each is appropriate, and can build a model whose feature tree is robust rather than merely correct on the first render.
- Solid parametric modeling fundamentals: fully-constrained sketching, datum planes and local coordinate systems, expressions and spreadsheet-driven parameters, and an understanding of how topological naming affects downstream references.
- Practical troubleshooting instincts — you can diagnose a failing constraint solver, an over-constrained sketch, a broken feature reference after an upstream edit, and a boolean that fails on non-manifold or self-intersecting geometry.
Working knowledge of at least two more FreeCAD workbenches relevant to real workflows (Assembly, TechDraw, Draft, Spreadsheet, FEM, or CAM/Path).
- File-format fluency: STEP, IGES, BREP, STL/mesh, and the practical consequences of moving between solid and mesh representations.
- A computer you can install our recording tools on and work in daily: Windows 11, Ubuntu (X11), or macOS. Batches are assigned by operating system, and hardware capable of running FreeCAD comfortably alongside a screen recorder is required.
- Comfort being screen-recorded while you work, and the discipline to keep personal information and any client-confidential geometry out of frame.
- English proficiency: minimum B2, with the written clarity to document a workflow another engineer can reproduce.
- Ability to apply detailed rubrics consistently and make repeatable quality judgments across many similar tasks.
- Highly detail-oriented and self-directed, with strong asynchronous work habits for remote, flexible-hour contract work.

Responsibilities:

- Develop AI Training Content: Create detailed prompts in various topics and responses to guide AI learning, ensuring the models reflect a comprehensive understanding of diverse subjects.
- Optimize AI Performance: Evaluate and rank AI responses to enhance the model's accuracy, fluency, and contextual relevance.
- Ensure Model Integrity: Test AI models for potential inaccuracies or biases, validating their reliability across use cases.

The current generation of AI agents can read a screen, but they still fail badly at doing real professional work inside real desktop software — and Blender is one of the hardest cases there is. Dense modal interfaces, keyboard-driven operators, a 3D viewport where the correct next click depends on the state of the mesh: agents that handle a web form competently fall apart on a modifier stack.

In this remote, hourly contract role you will help fix that. You will design realistic, challenging Blender tasks, then record yourself completing them on your own computer using recording tools we provide. title: FreeCAD / Mechanical CAD Expert, AI Computer-Use Trainer
description:
## About SME Careers

As AI systems become more sophisticated, they rely on human knowledge to better understand context and the world. At SME Careers, we partner with leading AI labs to improve how the next generation of intelligent systems learn, reason, and act. SME Careers is a fast-growing AI data services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate that provides AI training data to many of the world's top AI companies and foundation model labs. Your expertise in parametric CAD will directly help improve the world's premier AI models.

## About the Role

AI agents are getting good at reading a screen and clicking through web forms. Put one in front of a parametric CAD package and it falls apart. FreeCAD is an unforgiving test case: multiple workbenches with overlapping capabilities, a constraint solver that fails in ways the interface doesn't explain, feature histories where the correct next action depends entirely on what was built twenty steps earlier, and the topological naming problem lying in wait for anyone who references geometry carelessly. Engineering intent lives in the model tree, not on the screen — and that is exactly what current agents cannot see.

In this remote, hourly contract role you will help close that gap. You will design realistic, challenging CAD tasks, then record yourself completing them on your own computer using recording tools we provide. Each recording captures the full picture of how expert work actually gets done, the sequence of actions, the interface state at every step, and the files before and after, and becomes both a demonstration the model learns from and a benchmark it is measured against.

Because a model can only learn from work that can be scored, an equally important part of the job is defining what "done correctly" means. Alongside each task you will write the objective and the steps you took, and specify how the result should be verified, what the finished part, sketch, assembly, or drawing has to satisfy for the outcome to count as correct, and which intermediate checkpoints a partially-successful attempt would hit. In CAD this is a sharper question than it looks: a part can be dimensionally correct and still be wrong, because the sketch is under-constrained, the feature order won't survive a parameter change, or the model references a face that will migrate the moment anything upstream is edited. Encoding that distinction, dimensionally right versus actually right, is the contribution we need from you.

This position is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI data services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate that provides AI training data to many of the world's top AI companies and foundation model labs. Your work will directly help improve the world's premier AI models.

## What You'll Do
- Author production-realistic CAD tasks: Write task briefs reflecting work an engineering team would actually assign, model a part to a dimensioned drawing, build a parametric family driven by a spreadsheet, assemble components with mating constraints, produce a TechDraw sheet with sections and tolerances, prepare geometry for manufacture or export, scoped tightly enough that the outcome can be objectively verified.
- Record expert demonstrations: Set up your own environment for the task (reference drawings, source files, workbenches and add-ons in place) and record yourself executing it end to end with the provided capture tooling, producing a complete trace of actions, interface state, and file changes.-
- Document the workflow step by step: Log the steps you took in a form another engineer could follow and reproduce, in clear professional English.
- Define verification and success criteria: Specify what the finished model must satisfy, dimensional correctness, fully-constrained sketches, robust feature references, a tree that survives a parameter change, plus the intermediate milestones that mark real progress and the plausible wrong paths that should not be credited.
- Cover the range of difficulty: Produce tasks from single sketch-and-pad operations up to long, multi-step workflows that cross applications (a drawing opened from a PDF, dimensions pulled from a spreadsheet, output handed to a slicer, mesh or STEP data round-tripped from another tool).
- Review and quality-check others' work: For those who move into QA, audit submitted traces for task realism, recording completeness, step-to-action mapping, and whether the stated success criteria genuinely hold for the model produced.
- Work to project quality standards: Keep recordings free of personal information and confidential client geometry, use only approved applications, and complete all work using your own expertise, the use of closed-source AI assistants is contractually prohibited on this project.

## What You Bring
- 2–5 years of professional experience in mechanical design, product development, manufacturing engineering, or a comparable CAD-centric role (contract, studio, in-house, or freelance).
- Genuine FreeCAD proficiency, not just general CAD experience. You work fluently in Sketcher and Part Design, understand the difference between the Part and Part Design approaches and when each is appropriate, and can build a model whose feature tree is robust rather than merely correct on the first render.
- Solid parametric modeling fundamentals: fully-constrained sketching, datum planes and local coordinate systems, expressions and spreadsheet-driven parameters, and an understanding of how topological naming affects downstream references.
- Practical troubleshooting instincts — you can diagnose a failing constraint solver, an over-constrained sketch, a broken feature reference after an upstream edit, and a boolean that fails on non-manifold or self-intersecting geometry.
Working knowledge of at least two more FreeCAD workbenches relevant to real workflows (Assembly, TechDraw, Draft, Spreadsheet, FEM, or CAM/Path).
- File-format fluency: STEP, IGES, BREP, STL/mesh, and the practical consequences of moving between solid and mesh representations.
- A computer you can install our recording tools on and work in daily: Windows 11, Ubuntu (X11), or macOS. Batches are assigned by operating system, and hardware capable of running FreeCAD comfortably alongside a screen recorder is required.
- Comfort being screen-recorded while you work, and the discipline to keep personal information and any client-confidential geometry out of frame.
- English proficiency: minimum B2, with the written clarity to document a workflow another engineer can reproduce.
- Ability to apply detailed rubrics consistently and make repeatable quality judgments across many similar tasks.
- Highly detail-oriented and self-directed, with strong asynchronous work habits for remote, flexible-hour contract work.

Responsibilities:

- Develop AI Training Content: Create detailed prompts in various topics and responses to guide AI learning, ensuring the models reflect a comprehensive understanding of diverse subjects.
- Optimize AI Performance: Evaluate and rank AI responses to enhance the model's accuracy, fluency, and contextual relevance.
- Ensure Model Integrity: Test AI models for potential inaccuracies or biases, validating their reliability across use cases.

About the Role
In this hourly, remote contract role, you will review and compare AI-generated Python answers and Chinese-language explanations, evaluating reasoning quality and step-by-step problem-solving for correctness and clarity. - Ensure Model Integrity: Test AI models for potential inaccuracies or biases, validating their reliability across use cases.

- 1–5 years of relevant professional experience in Python development, code review, debugging, or technical problem solving.
- Minimum Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field or equivalent practical experience.
- Fluency in Mandarin Chinese, with the ability to interpret and evaluate technical content written in Chinese (Traditional Chinese preferred for HK).
- English proficiency: Minimum C1 level.
- Strong working knowledge of Python 3.x fundamentals (data structures, functions, modules, exceptions), plus practical debugging skills for real-world failures.
- Ability to evaluate solution quality using clear criteria (correctness, edge cases, complexity, readability) and apply rubrics consistently across many samples.

title: Malayalam Team Lead
description:
In this hourly, remote contractor role, you will work as a Malayalam Quality Assurance Lead (QAL) to oversee quality, consistency, and trainer performance across Malayalam AI training projects. You will review AI-generated Malayalam content and trainer/QA work, evaluate output quality against project guidelines, provide precise written feedback, and ensure that all contributors follow the expected quality standards.

You will assess work for accuracy, fluency, grammar, spelling, tone, cultural appropriateness, meaning preservation, instruction-following, formatting, and adherence to project-specific rubrics. You will spot recurring quality issues, communicate updates to trainers and QAs, support onboarding, maintain documentation, and help activate contributors who are not working consistently. This role requires strong Malayalam and English skills, excellent attention to detail, structured communication, and the ability to manage quality workflows across remote teams.

This role is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI Data Services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate, delivering training data for many of the world’s largest AI companies and foundation-model labs. Your Malayalam quality leadership will directly help improve the world’s premier AI models by ensuring that Malayalam training data is natural, accurate, culturally appropriate, well-documented, and aligned with client expectations.

Selection process involves an AI interview, a domain-specific task, and an interview with a recruiter.

Requirements:

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Malayalam, Linguistics, Translation, Communications, Journalism, English, Education, Quality Assurance, or a relevant domain/related field.
- Native or near-native Malayalam proficiency with strong reading and writing skills.
- Strong grasp of the English language to follow project guidelines, communicate with teams, and provide clear feedback in English.
- 3+ years of professional experience in Malayalam writing, editing, translation, localization, content QA, AI training, education, annotation, or related language-review workflows.
- Strong understanding of Malayalam grammar, spelling conventions, punctuation, tone, register, regional variation, and cultural context.
- Ability to evaluate Malayalam content against detailed rubrics and identify issues such as mistranslation, literal phrasing, unnatural tone, hallucinated claims, ambiguity, or inconsistent terminology.
- Experience leading or supporting remote teams of trainers, annotators, reviewers, editors, or QAs is strongly preferred.
- Comfortable working in fast-moving remote environments using tools such as Discord, Google Sheets, Google Docs, trackers, dashboards, and project management systems.
- Highly detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to maintain style guides, FAQs, trackers, onboarding materials, honeypots, and other quality documentation.
- Experience with AI training, data annotation, large language models, prompt/response evaluation, or rubric-based LLM QA is a strong plus.

Responsibilities:

- Quality monitoring: Spot-check Malayalam items, identify quality issues, provide ongoing feedback through DMs, and escalate recurring or critical issues.
- Trainer and QA communication: Update trainers and QAs on Discord about new item guidelines, project changes, workflow updates, and quality expectations.
- Question handling: Respond to trainer/QA questions clearly and promptly, especially around Malayalam wording, register, translation fidelity, cultural context, Kerala usage, diaspora usage, and edge cases.
- Trainer/QA activation management: DM contributors who are inactive or not working, encourage activation, track follow-ups, and flag availability issues when needed.
- Documentation: Create and maintain Malayalam project documentation, including style guides, trackers, FAQs, quality notes, examples, honeypots, and onboarding materials.
- Onboarding and training: Schedule and run onboarding/training calls with trainers and QAs to explain project expectations, workflows, rubrics, quality standards, and Malayalam-specific style requirements.
- Quality alignment: Ensure all trainers and QAs apply Malayalam language guidelines consistently and understand updates as projects evolve.
- Process improvement: Identify recurring quality gaps, propose workflow improvements, and help build scalable QA processes for Malayalam-language projects.

title: Thai Team Lead
description:
In this hourly, remote contractor role, you will work as a Thai Quality Assurance Lead (QAL) to oversee quality, consistency, and trainer performance across Thai AI training projects. You will review AI-generated Thai content and trainer/QA work, evaluate output quality against project guidelines, provide precise written feedback, and ensure that all contributors follow the expected quality standards.

You will assess work for accuracy, fluency, grammar, spelling, tone, cultural appropriateness, meaning preservation, instruction-following, formatting, and adherence to project-specific rubrics. You will spot recurring quality issues, communicate updates to trainers and QAs, support onboarding, maintain documentation, and help activate contributors who are not working consistently. This role requires strong Thai and English skills, excellent attention to detail, structured communication, and the ability to manage quality workflows across remote teams.

This role is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI Data Services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate, delivering training data for many of the world’s largest AI companies and foundation-model labs. Your Thai quality leadership will directly help improve the world’s premier AI models by ensuring that Thai training data is natural, accurate, culturally appropriate, well-documented, and aligned with client expectations.

Selection process involves an AI interview, a domain-specific task, and an interview with a recruiter.

Important:
There is no immediate project for this role; however, if qualified, you will be among the first experts we reach out to when relevant opportunities arise. This will also provide you with access to future projects available through our expert network.

Requirements:

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Thai, Linguistics, Translation, Communications, Journalism, English, Education, Quality Assurance, or a relevant domain/related field.
- Native or near-native Thai proficiency with strong reading and writing skills.
- Strong grasp of the English language to follow project guidelines, communicate with teams, and provide clear feedback in English.
- 3+ years of professional experience in Thai writing, editing, translation, localization, content QA, AI training, education, annotation, or related language-review workflows.
- Strong understanding of Thai grammar, spelling conventions, punctuation, tone, register, formal/informal usage, politeness markers, and cultural context.
- Ability to evaluate Thai content against detailed rubrics and identify issues such as mistranslation, literal phrasing, unnatural tone, incorrect register, hallucinated claims, ambiguity, or inconsistent terminology.
- Comfortable handling Thai-specific formatting and style issues, including word spacing, sentence flow, loanwords, honorifics, and audience-appropriate phrasing.
- Experience leading or supporting remote teams of trainers, annotators, reviewers, editors, or QAs is strongly preferred.
- Comfortable working in fast-moving remote environments using tools such as Discord, Google Sheets, Google Docs, trackers, dashboards, and project management systems.
- Highly detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to maintain style guides, FAQs, trackers, onboarding materials, honeypots, and other quality documentation.
- Experience with AI training, data annotation, large language models, prompt/response evaluation, or rubric-based LLM QA is a strong plus.

Responsibilities:

- Quality monitoring: Spot-check Thai items, identify quality issues, provide ongoing feedback through DMs, and escalate recurring or critical issues.
- Trainer and QA communication: Update trainers and QAs on Discord about new item guidelines, project changes, workflow updates, and quality expectations.
- Question handling: Respond to trainer/QA questions clearly and promptly, especially around Thai wording, tone, register, translation fidelity, cultural context, politeness level, formatting, and edge cases.
- Trainer/QA activation management: DM contributors who are inactive or not working, encourage activation, track follow-ups, and flag availability issues when needed.
- Documentation: Create and maintain Thai project documentation, including style guides, trackers, FAQs, quality notes, examples, honeypots, and onboarding materials.
- Onboarding and training: Schedule and run onboarding/training calls with trainers and QAs to explain project expectations, workflows, rubrics, quality standards, and Thai-specific style requirements.
- Quality alignment: Ensure all trainers and QAs apply Thai language guidelines consistently and understand updates as projects evolve.
- Process improvement: Identify recurring quality gaps, propose workflow improvements, and help build scalable QA processes for Thai-language projects.

title: Neuroscience Quality Assurance Lead (QAL)
description:
In this hourly, remote contractor role, you will work as a Neuroscience / Cognitive Science Quality Assurance Lead (QAL) to oversee quality, consistency, and trainer performance across neuroscience and cognitive science AI training projects. You will review AI-generated neuroscience/cognitive science content and trainer/QA work, evaluate output quality against project guidelines, provide precise written feedback, and ensure that all contributors follow the expected quality standards.

You will assess work for scientific accuracy, conceptual precision, research literacy, experimental-method understanding, brain-behavior reasoning, statistical caution, ethical awareness, clarity, formatting, instruction-following, and adherence to project-specific rubrics. You will spot recurring quality issues, communicate updates to trainers and QAs, support onboarding, maintain documentation, and help activate contributors who are not working consistently. This role requires strong neuroscience/cognitive science expertise, strong English communication skills, excellent attention to detail, structured communication, and the ability to manage quality workflows across remote expert teams.

This role is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI Data Services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate, delivering training data for many of the world’s largest AI companies and foundation-model labs. Your neuroscience/cognitive science quality leadership will directly help improve the world’s premier AI models by ensuring that scientific training data is accurate, evidence-aware, ethically appropriate, clearly explained, and aligned with client expectations.

Selection process involves an AI interview, a domain-specific task, and an interview with a recruiter.

Important:
There is no immediate project for this role; however, if qualified, you will be among the first experts we reach out to when relevant opportunities arise. This will also provide you with access to future projects available through our expert network.

Requirements:

- Bachelor’s, Master’s, PhD, MD/PhD, or equivalent professional background in Neuroscience, Cognitive Science, Psychology, Neurobiology, Cognitive Psychology, Computational Neuroscience, Neurology-adjacent research, Biology, Biomedical Sciences, or a closely related field.
- Strong grasp of the English language to follow project guidelines, communicate with teams, and provide clear written feedback.
- 3+ years of experience in neuroscience/cognitive science research, teaching, laboratory work, academic review, science communication, experimental design, data analysis, or related scientific workflows.
- Strong understanding of neural systems, cognition, perception, attention, memory, learning, language, decision-making, neuroanatomy, neural signaling, research methods, and brain-behavior relationships.
- Ability to evaluate neuroscience/cognitive science content against detailed rubrics and identify issues such as neuromyths, overclaiming, unsupported causal conclusions, flawed study interpretation, incorrect terminology, pseudoscience, or misleading clinical implications.
- Familiarity with tools or methods such as EEG, fMRI, behavioral experiments, computational modeling, neuropsychological assessment, statistics, Python/R/MATLAB, cognitive tasks, or literature review is preferred.
- Experience leading or supporting remote teams of researchers, reviewers, educators, annotators, science writers, or QAs is strongly preferred.
- Comfortable working in fast-moving remote environments using tools such as Discord, Google Sheets, Google Docs, trackers, dashboards, and project management systems.
- Highly detail-oriented and organized, with the ability to maintain style guides, FAQs, trackers, onboarding materials, calibration tasks, and documentation.
- Experience with AI training, data annotation, LLM evaluation, scientific QA, academic review, psychology/neuroscience content review, or rubric-based review is a strong plus.

Responsibilities:

- Quality monitoring: Spot-check neuroscience/cognitive science items, identify quality issues, provide ongoing feedback through DMs, and escalate recurring or critical issues.
- Scientific review: Evaluate AI-generated neuroscience/cognitive science explanations, research summaries, experimental interpretations, brain-behavior claims, cognitive theory applications, and step-by-step reasoning for accuracy and clarity.
- Trainer and QA communication: Update trainers and QAs on Discord about new item guidelines, project changes, workflow updates, quality expectations, and neuroscience/cognitive-science-specific review standards.
- Question handling: Respond to trainer/QA questions clearly and promptly, especially around neural mechanisms, cognition, experimental design, statistical interpretation, ethical boundaries, clinical caution, and rubric interpretation.
- Trainer/QA activation management: DM contributors who are inactive or not working, encourage activation, track follow-ups, and flag availability issues when needed.
- Documentation: Create and maintain neuroscience/cognitive science project documentation, including style guides, trackers, FAQs, quality notes, examples, honeypots, calibration tasks, and onboarding materials.
- Onboarding and training: Schedule and run onboarding/training calls with trainers and QAs to explain project expectations, workflows, rubrics, quality standards, and neuroscience/cognitive-science-specific review requirements.
- Quality alignment: Ensure all trainers and QAs apply neuroscience/cognitive science review guidelines consistently and understand updates as projects evolve.
- Safety and ethics review: Flag pseudoscientific, overconfident, clinically misleading, ethically problematic, or unsupported claims about the brain, cognition, behavior, or mental health.
- Process improvement: Identify recurring quality gaps, propose workflow improvements, and help build scalable QA processes for neuroscience/cognitive science AI training projects.

In this hourly, remote contractor role, you will work as a Medical Doctor (Specialist) Subject Matter Expert (SME) to review AI-generated clinical responses and/or create expert medical content, evaluating reasoning quality and step-by-step clinical problem-solving while providing precise written feedback. You will assess solutions for accuracy, clarity, safety, and adherence to the prompt; identify errors in clinical methodology, differential diagnosis, risk stratification, red-flag recognition, test interpretation, and treatment planning; fact-check medical information; write high-quality explanations and model solutions that demonstrate correct reasoning; and rate and compare multiple responses based on correctness and reasoning quality.

Board-certified/board-eligible specialists across a range of fields, including but not limited to Internal Medicine, Family Medicine, Emergency Medicine, Pediatrics, OB/GYN, Cardiology, Neurology, Psychiatry, General Surgery, Anesthesiology, Critical Care, Radiology, Oncology, Dermatology, Orthopedics, Gastroenterology, Pulmonology, Nephrology, Endocrinology, Infectious Disease, and Pathology are welcomed.

This role is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI Data Services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate, delivering training data for many of the world’s largest AI companies and foundation-model labs. Your healthcare expertise directly helps improve the world’s premier AI models by making their clinical and public-health reasoning more accurate, reliable, and clearly explained.

Important:
There is no immediate project for this role; however, if qualified, you will be among the first experts we reach out to when relevant opportunities arise. This will also provide you with access to future projects available through our expert network.

Requirements:

- MD/DO (or equivalent) with completed specialty training (residency/fellowship as applicable) and board eligibility/certification (or local equivalent).
- 5+ years of post-training clinical experience in a specialty setting (hospital, outpatient, academic, or community practice).
- Confident in advanced clinical reasoning: differential diagnosis, triage, red flags, and escalation pathways appropriate to specialty practice.
- Strong understanding of disease processes, guideline-based care, diagnostic pathways, and patient-safety considerations within your specialty.
- Exceptional attention to detail when fact-checking clinical content and identifying unsafe assumptions, missing contraindications, inappropriate tests/therapies, or misinterpretation of results; minimum C1 English proficiency.
- Comfortable evaluating answers for internal consistency (timelines, physiology, dosing/contraindications where relevant), appropriateness for setting (ED vs inpatient vs outpatient), and risk/benefit tradeoffs.
- Reliable, self-directed, and able to deliver consistent quality in an hourly, remote contractor workflow across time zones.
- Prior experience with AI data training/annotation, guideline work, utilization review, clinical documentation review, or healthcare editorial QA is strongly preferred.

Responsibilities:

- Develop AI Training Content: Create detailed prompts and gold-standard answers across clinical topics aligned to your specialty, ensuring accuracy and appropriate scope.
- Optimize AI Performance: Evaluate and rank AI responses to enhance correctness, safety, clarity, and contextual relevance.
- Ensure Model Integrity: Test AI outputs for inaccuracies, unsafe recommendations, and bias; validate reliability across use cases and patient populations.

As a C Engineer, you will work remotely on an hourly paid basis to review AI-generated C code, low-level systems designs, and technical explanations, as well as generate high-quality reference implementations and step-by-step reasoning for complex engineering problems. You will assess solutions for accuracy, clarity, safety, and adherence to the prompt; identify errors in logic, memory handling, concurrency, or performance; fact-check technical information; write high-quality explanations and model solutions that demonstrate correct methods; and rate and compare multiple AI responses based on correctness and reasoning quality. This fully remote, hourly paid contractor role is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI data services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate that provides AI training data to many of the world’s largest AI companies and foundation model labs. Your systems-level C expertise will directly help improve the world’s premier AI models used by millions of developers worldwide.

Important:
There is no immediate project for this role; however, if qualified, you will be among the first experts we reach out to when relevant opportunities arise. This will also provide you with access to future projects available through our expert network.

Requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree or higher in Computer Science, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or a closely related technical field.
- 4+ years of professional experience developing production software in C for systems, embedded, or performance-critical applications.
- Expert-level proficiency in C, including deep understanding of pointers, memory management, undefined behavior, and low-level debugging.
- Strong background in systems programming concepts such as concurrency, operating systems, hardware interaction, and performance optimization.
- Hands-on experience with build systems, compilers, linkers, and debugging tools commonly used in C development.
- Minimum C1 English proficiency (written and spoken), with the ability to write clear technical explanations and follow detailed English-language guidelines.
- Proven experience conducting detailed code reviews and enforcing coding standards for safety and maintainability in C codebases.
- Comfort working with version control, CI/CD workflows, and automated testing for C projects.
- Previous experience with AI data training, annotation, or evaluating AI-generated technical content is a strong plus.
- Highly detail-oriented and systematic, with a methodical approach to evaluating reasoning quality and identifying subtle issues in low-level code.

Responsibilities:

- Develop AI Training Content: Create detailed prompts in various topics and responses to guide AI learning, ensuring the models reflect a comprehensive understanding of diverse subjects.
- Optimize AI Performance: Evaluate and rank AI responses to enhance the model's accuracy, fluency, and contextual relevance.
- Ensure Model Integrity: Test AI models for potential inaccuracies or biases, validating their reliability across use cases.

In this hourly, remote contractor role, you will work as a Fintech / Crypto Subject Matter Expert (SME) to review AI-generated fintech, payments, and crypto/Web3 responses and/or create expert content, evaluating reasoning quality and step-by-step problem-solving while providing precise written feedback. You will assess solutions for accuracy, clarity, safety, and adherence to the prompt; identify errors in financial product logic, payments flows, blockchain/crypto concepts, custody and key management, smart-contract risk reasoning (conceptual), fraud/AML considerations, and regulatory-compliance awareness; fact-check technical and market concepts; write high-quality explanations and model solutions that demonstrate correct reasoning; and rate and compare multiple responses based on correctness and reasoning quality. This role is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI Data Services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate, delivering training data for many of the world’s largest AI companies and foundation-model labs.

Important:
There is no immediate project for this role; however, if qualified, you will be among the first experts we reach out to when relevant opportunities arise. This will also provide you with access to future projects available through our expert network.

Requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Finance, Economics, Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).
- 5+ years of professional experience in fintech, payments, banking, crypto, or adjacent domains (product, operations, risk, compliance, research, engineering, or consulting).
- Strong understanding of payments and money movement: authorization/settlement, chargebacks, fees, rails (card networks, ACH, wires), and common failure modes.
- Strong understanding of crypto/blockchain fundamentals: transaction lifecycle, consensus (high level), on-chain vs off-chain, token mechanics, and common misconceptions.
- Solid risk mindset: fraud vectors, account takeover, social engineering, custody/key management risks, and safety-first user guidance.
- Familiarity with compliance concepts relevant to fintech/crypto (high level): KYC/AML, sanctions awareness, consumer protection, and disclosure practices.
- Ability to evaluate answers for internal consistency (units, timelines, fees, security assumptions, and realistic constraints).
- Minimum C1 English proficiency with strong written communication and the ability to explain complex topics clearly.
- Reliable, self-directed, and able to deliver consistent quality in an hourly, remote contractor workflow across time zones.
- Prior experience with AI data training/annotation, financial content QA, risk/compliance review, or technical writing is strongly preferred.

Responsibilities:

- Develop AI Training Content: Create detailed prompts and gold-standard fintech/crypto outputs (explanations, scenario analyses, risk write-ups, user guidance).
- Optimize AI Performance: Evaluate and rank AI responses to improve correctness, clarity, safety, and practical usefulness.
- Ensure Model Integrity: Test AI outputs for inaccuracies, misleading certainty, unsafe financial guidance, and bias; validate reliability across use cases.

In this hourly, remote contractor role, you will work as a Fintech / Crypto Subject Matter Expert (SME) to review AI-generated fintech, payments, and crypto/Web3 responses and/or create expert content, evaluating reasoning quality and step-by-step problem-solving while providing precise written feedback. You will assess solutions for accuracy, clarity, safety, and adherence to the prompt; identify errors in financial product logic, payments flows, blockchain/crypto concepts, custody and key management, smart-contract risk reasoning (conceptual), fraud/AML considerations, and regulatory-compliance awareness; fact-check technical and market concepts; write high-quality explanations and model solutions that demonstrate correct reasoning; and rate and compare multiple responses based on correctness and reasoning quality. This role is with SME Careers, a fast-growing AI Data Services company and subsidiary of SuperAnnotate, delivering training data for many of the world’s largest AI companies and foundation-model labs.

Important:
There is no immediate project for this role; however, if qualified, you will be among the first experts we reach out to when relevant opportunities arise. This will also provide you with access to future projects available through our expert network.

Requirements:

- Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Finance, Economics, Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or a related field (or equivalent professional experience).
- 5+ years of professional experience in fintech, payments, banking, crypto, or adjacent domains (product, operations, risk, compliance, research, engineering, or consulting).
- Strong understanding of payments and money movement: authorization/settlement, chargebacks, fees, rails (card networks, ACH, wires), and common failure modes.
- Strong understanding of crypto/blockchain fundamentals: transaction lifecycle, consensus (high level), on-chain vs off-chain, token mechanics, and common misconceptions.
- Solid risk mindset: fraud vectors, account takeover, social engineering, custody/key management risks, and safety-first user guidance.
- Familiarity with compliance concepts relevant to fintech/crypto (high level): KYC/AML, sanctions awareness, consumer protection, and disclosure practices.
- Ability to evaluate answers for internal consistency (units, timelines, fees, security assumptions, and realistic constraints).
- Minimum C1 English proficiency with strong written communication and the ability to explain complex topics clearly.
- Reliable, self-directed, and able to deliver consistent quality in an hourly, remote contractor workflow across time zones.
- Prior experience with AI data training/annotation, financial content QA, risk/compliance review, or technical writing is strongly preferred.

Responsibilities:

- Develop AI Training Content: Create detailed prompts and gold-standard fintech/crypto outputs (explanations, scenario analyses, risk write-ups, user guidance).
- Optimize AI Performance: Evaluate and rank AI responses to improve correctness, clarity, safety, and practical usefulness.
- Ensure Model Integrity: Test AI outputs for inaccuracies, misleading certainty, unsafe financial guidance, and bias; validate reliability across use cases.

title: Financial Analyst
description:
In this hourly, remote contractor role, you will work as a Financial Analysis Subject Matter Expert (SME) to review AI-generated financial analysis and business-finance responses and/or create expert finance content, evaluating reasoning quality and step-by-step analytical problem-solving while providing precise written feedback. You will assess solutions for accuracy, clarity, and adherence to the prompt; identify errors in financial modeling logic, assumptions, unit economics, valuation reasoning, forecasting, and metric interpretation; fact-check finance concepts and calculations; write high-quality explanations and model solutions that demonstrate correct methods; and rate and compare multiple responses based on correctness and reasoning quality. - 5+ years of professional experience in financial analysis (FP&A, corporate finance, investment banking, equity research, consulting, or similar).
- Strong command of core finance concepts: 3-statement logic, cash flow drivers, working capital, margin analysis, capital allocation, and basic corporate accounting linkage.
- Proven experience building and reviewing financial models (forecasting, scenario/sensitivity analysis, cohort/unit economics, pricing/packaging analyses).
- Comfortable with valuation reasoning (DCF mechanics, comps selection, multiple drivers) and clearly stating assumptions and limitations.
- Strong quantitative rigor and attention to detail (units, sign conventions, time horizons, circularity, error-checks).
- Ability to communicate complex analyses clearly in writing (executive summary, key drivers, risks, recommendations); minimum C1 English proficiency.
- Reliable, self-directed, and able to deliver consistent quality in an hourly, remote contractor workflow across time zones.

- Develop AI Training Content: Create detailed prompts and gold-standard finance outputs (models, assumptions tables, narratives, sensitivity analyses, investment-style summaries).
- Optimize AI Performance: Evaluate and rank AI responses to improve numeric correctness, rigor, clarity, and practical usefulness.
- Ensure Model Integrity: Test AI outputs for calculation errors, misleading interpretations, unsafe assumptions, and bias; validate reliability across business scenarios.

- 5+ years of professional experience in contracts (in-house legal, law firm, procurement, vendor management, legal ops, or contracts management).
- Strong ability to identify and explain contract risk: liability caps, indemnities, warranties, limitations/exclusions, termination rights, payment risk, IP ownership/licensing.

- Ensure Model Integrity: Test AI outputs for inaccuracies, misleading certainty, confidentiality risks, and bias; validate reliability across contract scenarios.
